Assessor
What We Do
The Assessor is charged with placing a fair market value of property in St. Charles County for the purpose of property tax as of the tax date. The property tax in Missouri is based on property value.
Real estate values are reassessed every odd-numbered year. Personal property (vehicles, equipment, etc.) is reassessed each year. Information maintained by this office is for assessment purposes only and should not be used to verify or transfer ownership. All maps maintained, provided and/or purchased are based on assessment information and do not represent a legal survey of the parcels shown and shall not be used for conveyance or the establishment of property boundaries.
The office of Assessor is an elected position, meaning the Assessor works independently of any other elected officials or taxing jurisdictions.
We are not responsible for
Setting your tax rate or deciding how much you will be taxed. Tax rates are established by the legislative board of each individual taxing entity, then combined into one bill sent out by the Collector’s Office. Your tax bill includes a breakdown of each entity’s tax rate.
Collecting property taxes or disbursing them to tax-funded entities.
Who Decides My Taxes?
No single person or group is responsible for your tax bill. Different offices are given authority over different parts of the bill.
Assessment Authority
Taxing Authority
Collection Authority
Assessment Authority
The Assessor’s Office is responsible for identifying the fair market value of real estate and personal property within the county. These values are used to ensure the tax burden is distributed fairly among residents and property owners.
Taxing Authority
Entities that use tax revenues to provide public services (school districts, city governments, fire districts, etc.) decide their tax rates each year based on the budgetary requirements needed to appropriately fund those services. Each property owner in St. Charles County is subject to no fewer than six taxing jurisdictions (state, county, school, fire, ambulance, library), and often more, depending on where you live.
Collection Authority
The Collector’s Office is responsible for consolidating tax rates from each taxing entity into one bill, applying reductions from any property tax relief program(s), then collecting the appropriate amount of tax for each property.
Requesting RECA Documentation
To request documents from St. Charles County for Radiation Exposure Compensation Act (RECA) claims, please complete this form . St. Charles County can provide marriage records, deeds and/or voter registration records for these claims. Please be advised that requests may take up to 10 business days to complete.
Personal Property FAQs
How can I get a certificate of non-assessment/tax waiver?
A Certificate of Personal Property Non-Assessment may be obtained from the Assessor’s Office if you did not own a vehicle in St. Charles County on January 1 of the required tax year. Complete the online request form , or visit the Assessor’s Office at 201 N. Second St., St. Charles, MO 63301.
How much do I owe?
For an estimate for how much you might owe on your next tax bill, visit the Calculating Estimated Property Tax page.
How do I know if I filed my personal property assessment?
You can verify online , or call us at 636-949-7420.
What information do I need to complete my personal property assessment form?
For a vehicle: Year, make, model, VIN number, and mileage. This form must be completed each year.
When are personal property assessment forms due?
March 1 of each year.

Real Estate FAQs
Why is our property being reassessed?
Missouri law requires a re-evaluation of real estate property values every odd-numbered year. Personal property is assessed annually.
The purpose of real estate reassessment is to make sure each property is fairly valued based on the current market. This ensures the tax burden is distributed fairly among all property owners.
New construction is added to the tax rolls on an annual basis.
I have not done anything to my property, so why is the value changing?
Our assessments adjust based on the current real estate market for similar properties. Economic conditions that affect the value of homes or commercial properties will eventually be reflected in assessments. In other words, our assessments are based on what we think a property would sell for if it went on the market today.
What is market value?
Market value is the likely price a property would sell for in an open, competitive market. Not all sales are completed at market value.
How do you actually determine property values?
We collect and analyze a number of data points to estimate the market value of real estate:
Property type, such as commercial, industrial, residential, or agricultural
Physical measurements of each structure and improvement, checked multiple times using in-person measuring, building permits, aerial photography and sales data
Outside data sources including appraisals, real estate services, citizen input, and other government agencies
Geographic information such as zoning, road access, location and neighborhood
Sales data including the last sale price, current condition of the property, and sale price of similar properties in the surrounding area (excluding sales that are clearly much higher or lower than normal market value)
What is the difference between sale price, appraisal and assessments?
Sale price is the factual amount paid by a buyer for a property or group of properties.
Appraisal is a detailed, single-property estimate of value, used for private financial purposes.
Assessment is a mass appraisal of property, used for tax purposes. This process uses statistical analysis to estimate the value for groups of similar properties, rather than creating a highly detailed appraisal of a single property.

Before You Visit Our Office
If you need to visit us in person, please use the check-in kiosk in the lobby of the Administration Building to join the queue. You can view wait times and get in line before you arrive by checking in online during business hours. When it’s your turn, you will be directed to a service window or a staff member will meet you in the lobby to assist.
